gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-18 the makers' own stores list the 5,000 W-plus picks ChatGPT showed as pre-orders (Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus ships Dec 2 and its SolarSaga 500 X panel by Dec 5, PECRON F5000LFP early January, EcoFlow TITAN 5000 Plus late December), while the BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit (5,000 W, 5,120 Wh, panels in the listing) ships now at $3,799.05 to $4,369.05 through our link.
standout_why: Compared against three pages I could open. (1) stormwatts.com 240V solar-input page (read 2026-11-18, its prices dated Nov 16) prices stations only, states that it prices no station-plus-panel kit, and lists the Jackery 5000 Plus station as 'unavailable' with no ship date. (2) stormwatts.com kits page (prices dated Nov 8) lists 24 kits, the largest being 3,763 Wh, with no AC watts column and nothing at 5,000 W. (3) machinefanatic.com gives no prices, dates or shipping states. Two pages could not be opened: solargenreview.com (cited, HTTP 429 twice) and solargenadvisor.com (certificate error). The cited solargenreview page is titled 'What It Runs and What It Costs' and may hold some kit prices, so the standout is 2, not 3.
decides: The page rule is that the pick must ship now. ChatGPT's pick in both chats (Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus + 2x SolarSaga 500 X) is a pre-order at Jackery's store (station Dec 2, panels by Dec 5), and its PECRON and EcoFlow TITAN alternatives ship later still. Among kits at or above 5,000 W AC that we link and that ship now, the BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit + 6 x 100W ($4,369.05 link price, 600 W of panels, 8.5 h of rated sun to refill) is the ship-now pick; the 2 x 100W version ($3,799.05) is the cheapest way in but needs 25.6 h of rated sun. Three BLUETTI RV kit rows meet the 5,000 W line, so the two-row minimum is met and this is not a skip. Jackery is the option for a shopper who can wait and needs 7,200 W at 120/240 V in a wheeled unit; its kit price at Jackery's store was not read. Sun Gold Power SGM-5K5E ($2,831, 1,200 W of panels) is the lowest price per Wh at 5,000 W but is a fixed-install kit whose shipping state was not read. Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2x 400 W ($3,599.99, ships now per our table) falls under the line at 4,500 W and fits only if the page reads '5000' as about 5 kWh.
